-  We classified 11 files: 3 data, 4 code, 4 documentation.
-  We found 3 tabular data files and extracted 308 columns from 3 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3). We ran automated data-quality checks on 308 columns; 61 columns have at least one potential issue (49 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 8 columns with numeric values stored as text; 3 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 2 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 1 column with inconsistent category casing; 1 column whose values look like personal information). We detected demographic column for Age. 3 of 3 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: A-maze of Natural Stories: Comprehension and surprisal in the Maze task
papers.summary:
-  We classified 409 files: 81 data, 98 code, 146 documentation, 83 materials, 1 unknown.
-  We found 74 tabular data files and extracted 553 columns from 57 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 5 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  13 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (Analysis/models/gams_linearity_test.rds: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; Analysis/models/maze_model_compare.rds: 71% of columns are free text, not variables; Analysis/models/spr_model_compare.rds: 71% of columns are free text, not variables; G_data_1.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; G_data_2.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; L_data_1.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; L_data_2.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; SPR_data_1.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; SPR_data_2.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; frwac_vocab.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; vboyce/natural-stories-maze-v1.0.zip/vboyce-natural-stories-maze-dcfa4a2/Analysis/models/gams_linearity_test.rds: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; vboyce/natural-stories-maze-v1.0.zip/vboyce-natural-stories-maze-dcfa4a2/Analysis/models/maze_model_compare.rds: 71% of columns are free text, not variables; vboyce/natural-stories-maze-v1.0.zip/vboyce-natural-stories-maze-dcfa4a2/Analysis/models/spr_model_compare.rds: 71% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: Analysis/models/gams_linearity_test.rds, Analysis/models/maze_model_compare.rds, Analysis/models/spr_model_compare.rds, G_data_1.txt, G_data_2.txt, L_data_1.txt, L_data_2.txt, SPR_data_1.txt, SPR_data_2.txt, frwac_vocab.txt, vboyce/natural-stories-maze-v1.0.zip/vboyce-natural-stories-maze-dcfa4a2/Analysis/models/gams_linearity_test.rds, vboyce/natural-stories-maze-v1.0.zip/vboyce-natural-stories-maze-dcfa4a2/Analysis/models/maze_model_compare.rds, vboyce/natural-stories-maze-v1.0.zip/vboyce-natural-stories-maze-dcfa4a2/Analysis/models/spr_model_compare.rds. We ran automated data-quality checks on 553 columns; 42 columns have at least one potential issue (36 columns with inconsistent category casing; 4 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 4 columns whose values look like personal information; 4 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.

findings.label: Case issues

papers.summary:
-  We classified 255 files: 204 data, 8 code, 41 documentation, 1 materials, 1 unknown.
-  We found 106 tabular data files and extracted 1073 columns from 94 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex40).
-  12 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://osf.io/46cuq exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, 29 files omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1073 columns and found no issues.

-  We could not list every file of 2 repositories, so the checks did not see all their files: https://figshare.com/s/f5df316056b7d504660e (could not be listed: private share link (figshare.com/s/...) cannot be resolved without a browser); https://doi.org/10.25383/city.32051415 (could not be listed: unfound).
-  We classified 296 files: 59 data, 160 code, 69 documentation, 1 materials, 7 unknown.
-  We found 59 tabular data files and extracted 17102 columns from 58 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 19 study groups (ex1, ex10, ex11, ex1a, ex1b, ex2, ex3, ex3a, ex3b, ex3c, ex3d, ex4, ex5, ex6, ex7, ex8, ex9, ex99, ex9a), plus 6 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (exp11+(replication+of+exp10,+vivid+vs.+neutral)_December+4,+2025_00.20_responses.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: exp11+(replication+of+exp10,+vivid+vs.+neutral)_December+4,+2025_00.20_responses.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 17102 columns; 3470 columns have at least one potential issue (3405 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 52 columns whose name suggests personal information; 26 columns that look like geographic coordinates; 18 columns with inconsistent category casing; 18 columns with numeric values stored as text; 18 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 8 columns whose values look like personal information; 4 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 2 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column whose names become identical when special characters are removed). 1 survey respondent was flagged for possible careless responding. We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 20 files are a Qualtrics survey export (127 rows look like previews/unfinished responses to review). 11 of 11 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Home or Lab? Effects of Recording Environment and Experimenter Presence on Speech Production Acoustics
papers.summary:
-  We classified 26 files: 10 data, 6 code, 10 documentation.
-  We found 10 tabular data files and extracted 240 columns from 10 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 240 columns; 84 columns have at least one potential issue (74 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 10 columns with values in a legacy (non-UTF-8) encoding).

papers.title: Strategic Signaling: Cheap Talk and the Facets of Antagonism
papers.summary:
-  We classified 19 files: 3 data, 13 code, 2 documentation, 1 materials.
-  We found 3 tabular data files and extracted 117 columns from 3 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 117 columns; 53 columns have at least one potential issue (51 columns with numeric values stored as text; 3 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed).

papers.summary:
-  245 files could not be downloaded, so the checks did not see them.
-  We could not list every file of 1 repository, so the checks did not see all its files: https://osf.io/djv4e (could not be listed: private).
-  We classified 866 files: 741 data, 58 code, 9 documentation, 1 materials, 7 output, 50 unknown.
-  We found 433 tabular data files and extracted 864 columns from 139 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (pilot1), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  294 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://osf.io/smcau exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: fetched the smallest archive members up to the cap, 90 members omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more.

papers.title: Rethinking Smartphones and Sleep: A Fine-Grained Within-Person Analysis of Evening Smartphone Use and Sleep
papers.summary:
-  We classified 25 files: 5 data, 15 code, 5 documentation.
-  We found 5 tabular data files and extracted 1911 columns from 4 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4), plus 3 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (eMotion_sensing_feature_list.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: eMotion_sensing_feature_list.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1911 columns; 104 columns have at least one potential issue (77 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 16 columns with numeric values stored as text; 7 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 2 columns with inconsistent category casing; 2 columns whose name suggests personal information; 1 column whose values look like personal information; 1 column holding an SPSS "Select Cases" filter (analyses may have used only a subset of rows)). 347 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (57 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 3 of 3 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Impact of Exergames on Cognition in Midlife and Older Age: A Bayesian Meta-Analysis
papers.summary:
-  We classified 134 files: 86 data, 29 code, 16 documentation, 3 materials.
-  We found 86 tabular data files and extracted 819 columns from 19 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  35 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (Included_articles_references_DOI.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: Included_articles_references_DOI.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 819 columns; 67 columns have at least one potential issue (40 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 11 columns with inconsistent category casing; 10 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 3 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 2 columns whose values look like personal information; 2 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). We detected demographic column for Age. 3 of 3 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

-  We classified 650 files: 35 data, 7 code, 6 documentation, 598 materials, 4 unknown.

papers.title: The Allure of Simplicity: Framing Effects and Theoretical Virtues
papers.summary:
-  We classified 4 files: 3 data, 1 code.
-  We found 3 tabular data files and extracted 42 columns from 3 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3). We ran automated data-quality checks on 42 columns; 10 columns have at least one potential issue (7 columns with inconsistent category casing; 3 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 3 columns whose name suggests personal information; 3 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). We detected demographic columns for Gender, Race. 1 file is a Qualtrics survey export.

papers.title: The Forecasting Proficiency Test: A General Use Assessment of Forecasting Ability
papers.summary:
-  We classified 5077 files: 3198 data, 95 code, 46 documentation, 1737 materials, 1 unknown.
-  We found 2693 tabular data files and extracted 1602 columns from 52 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 7 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex8, pilot1, pilot1a, pilot2), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2638 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://github.com/forecastingresearch/fpt exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, 2643 files omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more.
-  1 R workspace file (`.RData`/`.rda`) contains no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: Forecasting Proficiency Test R Environment.RData.
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (data_cognitive_tasks/cache/session_info.RData: the file has no data rows or columns; data_pilot_cognitive_tasks/cache/session_info.RData: the file has no data rows or columns). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: data_cognitive_tasks/cache/session_info.RData, data_pilot_cognitive_tasks/cache/session_info.RData.
-  505 trial-level data files (E-Prime / Inquisit / jsPsych / Behaverse) were recognised. These are per-participant records of a behavioural task, so they are not listed as separate datasets. Nothing is deleted. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1602 columns; 26 columns have at least one potential issue (17 columns with numeric values stored as text; 8 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 6 columns whose name suggests personal information; 1 column with inconsistent category casing). 2 files are a Qualtrics survey export (696 rows look like previews/unfinished responses to review). 2 of 2 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: I Remember That Question: Using Eye Tracking to See How Prequestions Shape Reading
papers.summary:
-  We classified 578 files: 452 data, 25 code, 44 documentation, 55 materials, 1 output, 1 unknown.
-  We found 408 tabular data files and extracted 11757 columns from 347 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, pilot1), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (r_package_versions.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: r_package_versions.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 11757 columns; 562 columns have at least one potential issue (365 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 170 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 25 columns with inconsistent category casing; 1 column of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). 3 of 5 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Comparing physical literacy scores by sex and movement behaviour distributions across physical literacy profiles among elementary school students: an exploratory study
papers.summary:
-  We classified 1416 files: 1003 data, 9 code, 11 documentation, 206 materials, 101 output, 86 unknown.
-  We found 708 tabular data files and extracted 23049 columns from 510 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 5 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  Repository https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24053778 exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: fetched the smallest archive members up to the cap, 156 members omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more.
-  196 R workspace files (`.RData`/`.rda`) contain no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. -  We could not list every file of 1 repository, so the checks did not see all its files: https://osf.io/hnspm (could not be listed: closed registration source).

papers.title: Own and others' confidence in social information use
papers.summary:
-  We classified 216 files: 110 data, 47 code, 40 documentation, 16 materials, 3 output.
-  We found 110 tabular data files and extracted 3161 columns from 86 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 5 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4, pilot1), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 tabular data file could not be read because it was not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  10 R workspace files (`.RData`/`.rda`) contain no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: heuristics_condition_beast_random.RData, model_interaction_beast_full_treatments.RData, model_interaction_beast.RData, heuristics_condition_beast.RData, zoib_model_beast.RData, model_interaction_beast_full_scale.RData, model_interaction_beast_uncertainty.RData, heuristics_condition_elections_random.RData, model_interaction_elections.RData, heuristics_condition_elections.RData.
-  4 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (data/elections/clean_data/social_info/e1low.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; data/elections/clean_data/states_short.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; Confidence-Self-Others  OSF.zip/Confidence-Self-Others  OSF/data/elections/clean_data/states_short.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; Confidence-Self-Others  OSF.zip/Confidence-Self-Others  OSF/data/elections/clean_data/social_info/e1low.txt: the file has no data rows or columns). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: data/elections/clean_data/social_info/e1low.txt, data/elections/clean_data/states_short.txt, Confidence-Self-Others  OSF.zip/Confidence-Self-Others  OSF/data/elections/clean_data/states_short.txt, Confidence-Self-Others  OSF.zip/Confidence-Self-Others  OSF/data/elections/clean_data/social_info/e1low.txt. We ran automated data-quality checks on 3161 columns; 767 columns have at least one potential issue (562 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 96 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 77 columns with inconsistent category casing; 32 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 9 columns with numeric values stored as text; 9 columns whose values look like personal information; 7 columns whose name suggests personal information; 6 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 2 columns with values in a legacy (non-UTF-8) encoding; 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 11 of 15 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: From the app to the lexicon: Neurocognitive markers of word integration in a second language
papers.summary:
-  We classified 85 files: 74 data, 4 code, 7 documentation.
-  We found 29 tabular data files and extracted 5666 columns from 29 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 5666 columns; 1735 columns have at least one potential issue (1403 columns with numeric values stored as text; 331 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). We detected demographic column for Age. 24 of 26 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Neural evidence for intact statistical learning in Developmental Dyslexia in the absence of conclusive behavioral results: an individual differences approach to cognitive correlates
papers.summary:
-  We could not list every file of 1 repository, so the checks did not see all its files: OSF.IO/Model (could not be listed: not found on the OSF (HTTP 404)).
-  We classified 371 files: 250 data, 21 code, 14 documentation, 83 materials, 3 output.
-  We found 248 tabular data files and extracted 176 columns from 8 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  225 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/HU6VM exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, 149 files omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more.

papers.summary:
-  We classified 30 files: 8 data, 3 code, 11 documentation, 8 materials.
-  We found 8 tabular data files and extracted 413 columns from 7 of them.

No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: S1 SOM correlations.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 413 columns; 122 columns have at least one potential issue (48 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 45 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 42 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 18 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 17 columns whose name suggests personal information; 11 columns with inconsistent category casing; 4 columns that look like geographic coordinates). 105 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (76 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 2 files are a Qualtrics survey export (25 rows look like previews/unfinished responses to review). 1 of 1 spreadsheet file has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Humans adaptively delay planning using cognitive maps
papers.summary:
-  We could not list every file of 1 repository, so the checks did not see all its files: https://osf.io/kca68 (could not be listed: private).
-  We classified 1018 files: 592 data, 213 code, 21 documentation, 188 materials, 4 unknown.
-  We found 536 tabular data files and extracted 74455 columns from 528 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex2, ex3, pilot1, pilot3).
-  8 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/best_subs.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/borderline_subs.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/not_planned/good_subs.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/bad_subs.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/best_subs.csv #1: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/borderline_subs.csv #1: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/not_planned/good_subs.csv #1: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/bad_subs.csv #1: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/best_subs.csv, tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/borderline_subs.csv, tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/not_planned/good_subs.csv, tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/bad_subs.csv, tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/best_subs.csv #1, tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/borderline_subs.csv #1, tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/not_planned/good_subs.csv #1, tqckj: Study1_n67_LearnToPlan.zip/full_study_3step/bad_subs.csv #1. We ran automated data-quality checks on 74455 columns; 147 columns have at least one potential issue (111 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 36 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long).

papers.title: Perceptual distinctiveness underlies apparent emotion-specific advantages in facial expression detection
papers.summary:
-  We classified 1822 files: 1811 data, 8 code, 1 documentation, 2 materials.
-  We found 1206 tabular data files and extracted 10854 columns from 1206 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 10854 columns; 1206 columns have at least one potential issue (603 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 603 columns whose name suggests personal information). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.

-  We found 15 tabular data files and extracted 644 columns from 15 of them.

We ran automated data-quality checks on 644 columns; 77 columns have at least one potential issue (69 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 8 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed). 15 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding. We detected demographic column for Gender.

papers.title: A mind-body disconnection? Discordance between thoughts about stress and cardiovascular stress responses
papers.summary:
-  We classified 68 files: 19 data, 11 code, 1 documentation, 32 materials, 5 output.
-  We found 19 tabular data files and extracted 1537 columns from 19 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 5 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4, ex5). We ran automated data-quality checks on 1537 columns; 70 columns have at least one potential issue (45 columns with numeric values stored as text; 17 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 5 columns whose values look like personal information; 5 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns with inconsistent category casing; 1 column with leading/trailing whitespace). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 3 of 3 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Benchmarking an automated speech recognition pipeline for Spanish-English bilingual preschoolers: Quantifying language input and output in daylong recordings.
papers.summary:
-  We classified 106 files: 26 data, 73 code, 6 documentation, 1 materials.
-  We found 25 tabular data files and extracted 1146 columns from 24 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 6 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (recording_id_map.example.csv: the file has no data rows or columns). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: recording_id_map.example.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1146 columns; 964 columns have at least one potential issue (944 columns with numeric values stored as text; 20 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). 3 of 3 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Developing human-AI complementarity: Augmenting everyday decision making with Large Language Models
papers.summary:
-  We classified 10 files: 4 data, 6 materials.
-  We found 4 tabular data files and extracted 771 columns from 4 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3). We ran automated data-quality checks on 771 columns; 639 columns have at least one potential issue (535 columns with numeric values stored as text; 98 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 18 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 4 columns with inconsistent category casing). 18 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (18 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). 4 of 4 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: From use perception to use behavior: Digitally traced smartphone use purposes and psychological well-being in daily life
papers.summary:
-  We classified 9 files: 3 data, 1 code, 5 documentation.
-  We found 3 tabular data files and extracted 1811 columns from 2 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (eMotion_sensing_feature_list.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: eMotion_sensing_feature_list.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1811 columns; 102 columns have at least one potential issue (77 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 16 columns with numeric values stored as text; 7 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 2 columns with inconsistent category casing; 1 column whose values look like personal information; 1 column holding an SPSS "Select Cases" filter (analyses may have used only a subset of rows)). 347 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (57 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 5 of 5 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: The Dutch Gambling Harms Question Inventory (D-GHQI-12): 	 Development, psychometric properties and test-retest reliability
papers.summary:
-  We classified 25 files: 15 data, 3 code, 6 documentation, 1 output.
-  We found 15 tabular data files and extracted 2023 columns from 15 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex5). We ran automated data-quality checks on 2023 columns; 129 columns have at least one potential issue (85 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 35 columns with inconsistent category casing; 4 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 3 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). 2350 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (1595 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 5 of 5 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Tales of Life: Curiosity for Positive and Negative Life Stories of Culturally Close and Distant Others
papers.summary:
-  We classified 6 files: 4 data, 1 code, 1 documentation.
-  We found 4 tabular data files and extracted 1513 columns from 4 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2). We ran automated data-quality checks on 1513 columns; 1038 columns have at least one potential issue (1038 columns with numeric values stored as text). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 1 of 4 spreadsheet files has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 1 of 1 spreadsheet file has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Tracking the Integration of Novel Words into the Mental Lexicon: Evidence from Mouse Movement Trajectories
papers.summary:
-  We classified 66 files: 30 data, 8 code, 9 documentation, 18 materials, 1 unknown.
-  We found 30 tabular data files and extracted 4358 columns from 23 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 R workspace files (`.RData`/`.rda`) contain no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: data_trim.RData, data_trim_filtered.RData. We ran automated data-quality checks on 4358 columns; 2683 columns have at least one potential issue (2683 columns with no observed values (entirely empty)).

papers.title: A Multilevel Signal Detection Theory Approach to Unconscious Processing Research
papers.summary:
-  We classified 797 files: 542 data, 85 code, 32 documentation, 136 materials, 2 unknown.
-  We found 542 tabular data files and extracted 6838 columns from 530 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 5 study groups (ex1, ex1c, ex2, ex2a, ex3), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  6 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy. We ran automated data-quality checks on 6838 columns; 474 columns have at least one potential issue (327 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 62 columns whose values look like personal information; 56 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 27 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 4 columns with numeric values stored as text).

papers.title: Norms for Gender-Inclusive Role Nouns in Italian: The GIRN-I Database
papers.summary:
-  We classified 61 files: 39 data, 2 code, 18 documentation, 2 materials.
-  We found 39 tabular data files and extracted 12008 columns from 39 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 12008 columns; 107 columns have at least one potential issue (63 columns with inconsistent category casing; 25 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 17 columns with numeric values stored as text; 2 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). 1 survey respondent was flagged for possible careless responding. We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 18 files are a Qualtrics survey export.

papers.title: On Bias in Detecting Bias: A Signal Detection Analysis of Attributions to Gender Discrimination
papers.summary:
-  We classified 339 files: 42 data, 17 code, 24 documentation, 256 materials.
-  We found 38 tabular data files and extracted 155 columns from 12 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 6 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4, ex5, pilot1), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  4 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://osf.io/6cgxv/?view_only=370994d8777d48cd8989a488f7f27c29 exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, 3 files omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more.
-  1 trial-level data file (E-Prime / Inquisit / jsPsych / Behaverse) was recognised. These are per-participant records of a behavioural task, so they are not listed as separate datasets. Nothing is deleted. We ran automated data-quality checks on 155 columns; 17 columns have at least one potential issue (16 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 1 column with inconsistent category casing; 1 column with leading/trailing whitespace). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 1 .rds file was saved with save() instead of saveRDS(), so readRDS() cannot open it; rename it to .RData: demo.rds.

papers.summary:

papers.title: The Effects of Negative Affect and Dispositional Pessimism on Decision-Making Under Ambiguity
papers.summary:
-  We classified 50 files: 32 data, 17 code, 1 documentation.
-  We found 26 tabular data files and extracted 388 columns from 25 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 tabular data file could not be read because it was not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy. We ran automated data-quality checks on 388 columns; 74 columns have at least one potential issue (50 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 12 columns with numeric values stored as text; 10 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns with inconsistent category casing; 2 columns that look like geographic coordinates). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.

papers.title: Inequality Can Increase Stealing, Reduce Trust, and Undermine Cooperation, Even When It Is Invisible
papers.summary:
-  **We found 101 keys** (such as an API key or an access token) in 18 files. Anyone who downloads these files can use the service at the authors' cost.
-  We classified 4899 files: 14 data, 128 code, 117 documentation, 4640 materials.
-  We found 8 tabular data files and extracted 843 columns from 6 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2). We ran automated data-quality checks on 843 columns; 124 columns have at least one potential issue (102 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 20 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 18 columns with inconsistent category casing; 8 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 2 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.

papers.title: Beyond Consequences of Challenge: the Degree to which Spoken Word Recognition Changes in Response to Difficulty has Independent Relevance
papers.summary:
-  We classified 9 files: 7 data, 2 code.
-  We found 6 tabular data files and extracted 28 columns from 3 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1).
-  3 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (data.zip/osf/IEEE/avg_scores.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; data.zip/osf/Stroop/avg_scores.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; interpolated_data.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: data.zip/osf/IEEE/avg_scores.csv, data.zip/osf/Stroop/avg_scores.csv, interpolated_data.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 28 columns and found no issues. We detected demographic column for Age. 3 .csv files are separated by spaces instead of commas, so their columns could not be checked; save them as comma-separated .csv (or tab-separated .tsv): data.zip/osf/IEEE/avg_scores.csv, data.zip/osf/Stroop/avg_scores.csv, interpolated_data.csv.

findings.detail: This file is separated by spaces, not commas, so it reads as a single column and its columns could not be checked. papers.title: When Does Reputation Help the Future? Audience Presence and Identity Disclosure in Intergenerational Resource Dilemmas
papers.summary:
-  We classified 55 files: 37 data, 13 code, 5 documentation.
-  We found 22 tabular data files and extracted 195 columns from 20 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (sessionInfo.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; S_svo_corrections.csv: the file has no data rows or columns). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: sessionInfo.txt, S_svo_corrections.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 195 columns and found no issues. 1 survey respondent was flagged for possible careless responding (1 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.

papers.title: What Is a “Blank” Mind? Testing the Meaning and Construct Validity of Mind-Blanking Reports to Thought Probes
papers.summary:
-  We classified 48 files: 37 data, 8 code, 3 documentation.
-  We found 37 tabular data files and extracted 1029 columns from 29 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex1a, ex1b, ex2, ex3), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  8 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1029 columns; 161 columns have at least one potential issue (94 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 29 columns whose name suggests personal information; 28 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 13 columns with numeric values stored as text; 7 columns with inconsistent category casing; 6 columns that look like geographic coordinates; 3 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 2 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed). We detected demographic columns for Gender, Race.

-  1 file is a Git LFS pointer: the repository holds a small text file in place of the file itself, which was not deposited, so the checks did not see it.
-  We classified 2781 files: 11 data, 17 code, 4 documentation, 2 materials, 8 output, 2739 unknown.
-  We found 10 tabular data files and extracted 566 columns from 8 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (Macrosurvey samples by category.xlsx: 48% of columns are free text and 71% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset; data/_osf_backup/Macrosurvey samples by category.xlsx: 48% of columns are free text and 71% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: Macrosurvey samples by category.xlsx, data/_osf_backup/Macrosurvey samples by category.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 566 columns; 252 columns have at least one potential issue (102 columns with numeric values stored as text; 88 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 50 columns with inconsistent category casing; 16 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 10 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 8 columns of free text that may contain personal detail). 6 of 8 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 6 files: 4 data, 1 code, 1 documentation.
-  We found 4 tabular data files and extracted 259 columns from 4 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 259 columns; 42 columns have at least one potential issue (16 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 11 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 8 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 7 columns whose name suggests personal information; 4 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 4 columns with numeric values stored as text; 3 columns whose values look like personal information; 1 column with inconsistent category casing). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 2 files are a Qualtrics survey export (20 rows look like previews/unfinished responses to review).

papers.title: Emoticon variation: Eyes, mouths, and mirrorings are more meaningful than noses and rotations
papers.summary:
-  We classified 53 files: 19 data, 1 documentation, 33 materials.
-  We found 19 tabular data files and extracted 212 columns from 19 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 212 columns; 94 columns have at least one potential issue (85 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 29 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 19 columns with inconsistent category casing). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 19 of 19 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Towards a conceptual clarification and possible applications of Meehl’s crud factor: A preregistered systematic review
papers.summary:
-  We classified 59 files: 32 data, 8 code, 5 documentation, 14 unknown.
-  We found 30 tabular data files and extracted 781 columns from 23 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2).
-  7 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (Archive of OSF Storage/Data Transformations and Analyses/Preliminary Research/Extraction Document.xlsx: 56% of columns are free text and 62% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset; main folder/data/Extraction Document.xlsx: 44% of columns are free text and 69% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset; Inclusion List.xlsx: 52% of columns are free text and 68% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset; Extraction Document_Pre_Consensus.xlsx: 50% of columns are free text and 63% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset; input_effect_sizes.xlsx: 48% of columns are free text and 66% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset; crud_estimate_-Lykken.xlsx: 75% of columns are free text, not variables; crud_factor_-Lykken.xlsx: 75% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: Archive of OSF Storage/Data Transformations and Analyses/Preliminary Research/Extraction Document.xlsx, main folder/data/Extraction Document.xlsx, Inclusion List.xlsx, Extraction Document_Pre_Consensus.xlsx, input_effect_sizes.xlsx, crud_estimate_-Lykken.xlsx, crud_factor_-Lykken.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 781 columns; 161 columns have at least one potential issue (110 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 42 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 15 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 12 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 10 columns with numeric values stored as text; 7 columns whose values look like personal information; 6 columns with inconsistent category casing). 14 of 31 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Human Category Learning in Reversal Tasks: Dynamic Learning Rates Help Overcome Catastrophic Interference in Connectionist Networks
papers.summary:
-  We could not list every file of 1 repository, so the checks did not see all its files: https://github.com/santiagocdo/categorySimilarityicalReversalLerning (could not be listed: invalid or inaccessible GitHub repository).
-  We classified 211 files: 137 data, 26 code, 19 documentation, 26 materials, 1 output, 2 unknown.
-  We found 137 tabular data files and extracted 6395 columns from 134 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 18 study groups (ex1, ex10, ex11, ex12, ex13, ex14, ex15, ex16, ex1a, ex1b, ex2, ex3, ex4, ex5, ex6, ex7, ex8, ex9), plus 3 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  3 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (CRL1_task.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; design_task.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; design_task_debug.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: CRL1_task.csv, design_task.csv, design_task_debug.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 6395 columns; 817 columns have at least one potential issue (514 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 324 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 26 columns with numeric values stored as text; 5 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 3 of 3 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Where human similarity holds and where it breaks: Evaluating the alignment of synthetic focus groups
papers.summary:
-  We classified 1961 files: 1191 data, 400 code, 233 documentation, 24 materials, 102 output, 11 unknown.
-  We found 145 tabular data files and extracted 1595 columns from 117 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (pilot01, pilot02, pilot1, pilot20), plus 18 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  22 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (metric_registry_proposed_rows.csv: 70% of columns are free text, not variables; OCA-001_adjudication.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg1/front_matter.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg1/raw_extracted_transcript.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg2/front_matter.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg2/raw_extracted_transcript.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg3/front_matter.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg3/raw_extracted_transcript.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg4/clean_transcript.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg4/front_matter.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg4/transcript.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg5/clean_transcript.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg5/front_matter.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg5/raw_extracted_transcript.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg5/transcript.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; corpus_comparison_manifest.csv: 70% of columns are free text, not variables; smoke_test_artifact_issue_log.csv: the file has no data rows or columns; summary_by_condition.csv: 73% of columns are free text, not variables; transferability/another_discussion_guide/data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/mindfulness/fg1/clean_transcript.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; transferability/another_discussion_guide/data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/mindfulness/fg1/front_matter.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; transferability/another_discussion_guide/data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/mindfulness/fg1/raw_extracted_transcript.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; transferability/another_discussion_guide/data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/mindfulness/fg1/transcript.txt: the file has no data rows or columns). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: metric_registry_proposed_rows.csv, OCA-001_adjudication.xlsx, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg1/front_matter.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg1/raw_extracted_transcript.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg2/front_matter.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg2/raw_extracted_transcript.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg3/front_matter.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg3/raw_extracted_transcript.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg4/clean_transcript.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg4/front_matter.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg4/transcript.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg5/clean_transcript.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg5/front_matter.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg5/raw_extracted_transcript.txt, data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/macho_meals/fg5/transcript.txt, corpus_comparison_manifest.csv, smoke_test_artifact_issue_log.csv, summary_by_condition.csv, transferability/another_discussion_guide/data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/mindfulness/fg1/clean_transcript.txt, transferability/another_discussion_guide/data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/mindfulness/fg1/front_matter.txt, transferability/another_discussion_guide/data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/mindfulness/fg1/raw_extracted_transcript.txt, transferability/another_discussion_guide/data/datasets_transcripts/standardized/mindfulness/fg1/transcript.txt. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1595 columns; 196 columns have at least one potential issue (111 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 58 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 14 columns with numeric values stored as text; 9 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 4 columns with inconsistent category casing; 3 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). 21 of 22 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: NICE’s 2026 Consultation Draft Guideline for OCD and BDD (GID-NG10435): A Critical Appraisal with Secondary Analysis of NICE’s Published Data
papers.summary:
-  We classified 1 file: 1 data.
-  We found 1 tabular data file and extracted 108 columns from 1 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 108 columns; 76 columns have at least one potential issue (62 columns with numeric values stored as text; 11 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 3 columns of free text that may contain personal detail). 1 of 1 spreadsheet file has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 13 files: 8 data, 2 code, 3 documentation.
-  We found 8 tabular data files and extracted 421 columns from 8 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 421 columns; 24 columns have at least one potential issue (24 columns with numeric values stored as text; 4 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). 926 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (665 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). 8 files are a Qualtrics survey export (185 rows look like previews/unfinished responses to review). 4 of 4 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Methodological Flexibility in the Iowa Gambling Task Undermines Interpretability: A Meta-method Review
papers.summary:
-  We classified 266 files: 112 data, 82 code, 66 documentation, 4 materials, 2 unknown.
-  We found 112 tabular data files and extracted 3462 columns from 79 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  27 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  4 R workspace files (`.RData`/`.rda`) contain no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: vbgeu: data/raw/multiverse/IGTdata.rdata, igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/multiverse/IGTdata.rdata, vbgeu: IGTdataSteingroever2014.zip/IGTdataSteingroever2014/IGTdata.rdata, igt-methodological-flexibility: IGTdataSteingroever2014.zip/IGTdataSteingroever2014/IGTdata.rdata.
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/metamethod review/matching of scores/scores_r2_matched.xlsx: 43% of columns are free text and 43% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset; igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/multiverse/data source.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/metamethod review/matching of scores/scores_r2_matched.xlsx, igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/multiverse/data source.txt. We ran automated data-quality checks on 3462 columns; 315 columns have at least one potential issue (88 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 76 columns with numeric values stored as text; 74 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 66 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 7 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 4 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). 12 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding. 26 of 42 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Respiratory Phase and Visuospatial Attention: A Replication and Extension
papers.summary:
-  We classified 346 files: 330 data, 11 code, 5 documentation.
-  We found 325 tabular data files and extracted 13288 columns from 314 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 13288 columns; 305 columns have at least one potential issue (276 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 18 columns with numeric values stored as text; 11 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long).

papers.title: A Meta-Analysis of Psychosocial Interventions to Improve Students’ STEM Motivation.
papers.summary:
-  We classified 90 files: 68 data, 12 code, 8 documentation, 2 materials.
-  We found 58 tabular data files and extracted 1364 columns from 54 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (overview?view_only=cee939c3d42c42b69dd2abff42092f48: Data and Analysis.zip/OSF_Study1/tables/text_descriptives.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; zc9wg: Data and Analysis.zip/OSF_Study1/tables/text_descriptives.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: overview?view_only=cee939c3d42c42b69dd2abff42092f48: Data and Analysis.zip/OSF_Study1/tables/text_descriptives.csv, zc9wg: Data and Analysis.zip/OSF_Study1/tables/text_descriptives.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1364 columns; 76 columns have at least one potential issue (46 columns with numeric values stored as text; 10 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 8 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 6 columns with inconsistent category casing; 4 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 2 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). We detected demographic columns for Age, Race. 2 of 8 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Analyzing Binary Judgments: An Empirical and Simulation-Based Comparison of Aggregated and Trial-Level Approaches for Hypothesis Testing
papers.summary:
-  We classified 104 files: 66 data, 12 code, 26 documentation.
-  We found 66 tabular data files and extracted 577 columns from 64 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 tabular data file could not be read because it was not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  1 R workspace file (`.RData`/`.rda`) contains no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: full-results.Rda. We ran automated data-quality checks on 577 columns; 52 columns have at least one potential issue (38 columns with values in a legacy (non-UTF-8) encoding; 14 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 3 columns with leading/trailing whitespace).

papers.title: Rhythm of Thought: Tracing the Dynamics of Deliberation in Reasoning
papers.summary:
-  We classified 3518 files: 2222 data, 1144 code, 6 documentation, 144 output, 2 unknown.
-  We found 58 tabular data files and extracted 990 columns from 56 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://github.com/Jeremie-Beucler/Rythm-of-thought exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, 6 files omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more. We ran automated data-quality checks on 990 columns; 126 columns have at least one potential issue (62 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 56 columns with inconsistent category casing; 8 columns with numeric values stored as text; 4 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 4 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 1 column whose name suggests personal information). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 6 of 8 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Mechanical and Psychological Domains of Thought are Analogically Asymmetrical
papers.summary:
-  We classified 41 files: 24 data, 15 code, 1 documentation, 1 materials.
-  We found 24 tabular data files and extracted 541 columns from 24 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 541 columns; 65 columns have at least one potential issue (36 columns whose name suggests personal information; 30 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 12 columns that look like geographic coordinates; 11 columns whose values look like personal information; 7 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 6 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 4 columns with numeric values stored as text; 1 column with inconsistent category casing). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 6 files are a Qualtrics survey export (2 rows look like previews/unfinished responses to review).

papers.title: I Remember That Question: Using Eye Tracking to See How Prequestions Shape Reading
papers.summary:
-  We classified 578 files: 452 data, 25 code, 44 documentation, 55 materials, 1 output, 1 unknown.
-  We found 408 tabular data files and extracted 11757 columns from 347 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, pilot1), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (r_package_versions.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: r_package_versions.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 11757 columns; 562 columns have at least one potential issue (365 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 170 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 25 columns with inconsistent category casing; 1 column of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). 3 of 5 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: From Data to Dialogue: Using Person-Specific Networks to Personalize Cognitive-Behavioral Treatment for Chronic Pain
papers.summary:
-  We classified 70 files: 10 data, 9 code, 50 documentation, 1 materials.
-  We found 10 tabular data files and extracted 1719 columns from 10 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3). We ran automated data-quality checks on 1719 columns; 58 columns have at least one potential issue (17 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 16 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 14 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 9 columns with inconsistent category casing; 6 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 4 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns with numeric values stored as text; 2 columns whose name suggests personal information). 8 of 12 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

-  We classified 3448 files: 284 data, 1096 code, 367 documentation, 1581 materials, 8 output, 112 unknown.
-  We found 190 tabular data files and extracted 1311 columns from 103 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 5 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4, ex5), plus 67 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).

-  We classified 231 files: 111 data, 98 code, 22 documentation.
-  We found 106 tabular data files and extracted 2288 columns from 97 of them.

No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: validation_pp.csv, OSF_package_2026-10-19.zip/OSF_package_2026-10-19/1_revision_pipeline/data/experiment_2_Kirk/hallucination_kirk_alive.csv, OSF_package_2026-10-19.zip/OSF_package_2026-10-19/2_original_analyses/experiment_2_Kirk/hallucination_kirk_alive.csv, disaggregated_chats.csv, sentence_split_CLAUDE.csv, sentence_split_classic_CLAUDE.csv, sentence_split_kirk_CLAUDE.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 2288 columns; 466 columns have at least one potential issue (267 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 240 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 103 columns with inconsistent category casing; 29 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 16 columns with numeric values stored as text; 6 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). papers.summary:
-  We classified 821 files: 673 data, 47 code, 5 documentation, 94 materials, 2 unknown.
-  We found 611 tabular data files and extracted 5549 columns from 47 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 7 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4, ex5, ex6, pilot1), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  560 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://osf.io/9yvxt exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: fetched the smallest archive members up to the cap, 560 members omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more.
-  4 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (ProjectLog_20250411.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; ProjectLog_20250414.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; ProjectLog_20250426.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; ProjectLog_20250904.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: ProjectLog_20250411.txt, ProjectLog_20250414.txt, ProjectLog_20250426.txt, ProjectLog_20250904.txt. We ran automated data-quality checks on 5549 columns; 1793 columns have at least one potential issue (1793 columns with no observed values (entirely empty)). We detected demographic columns for Gender, Race.

papers.summary:

papers.title: Procedural learning in the serial reaction time task in individuals with and without Dyslexia: group-level and individual differences
papers.summary:
-  We classified 32 files: 28 data, 4 code.
-  We found 28 tabular data files and extracted 525 columns from 26 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex4).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (excluded_participants_study4.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; excluded_participants_study4.attention.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: excluded_participants_study4.csv, excluded_participants_study4.attention.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 525 columns; 146 columns have at least one potential issue (142 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns with inconsistent category casing; 2 columns with no observed values (entirely empty)). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.

papers.summary:
-  We classified 35 files: 19 data, 3 code, 13 documentation.
-  We found 18 tabular data files and extracted 4512 columns from 18 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 4512 columns; 526 columns have at least one potential issue (339 columns with numeric values stored as text; 107 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 51 columns with inconsistent category casing; 22 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 20 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 12 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns whose name suggests personal information). 7379 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (3802 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 6 files are a Qualtrics survey export (2 rows look like previews/unfinished responses to review).

papers.title: Conspiratorial echoes of disease: The relationship between pathogen prevalence and conspiracy beliefs
papers.summary:
-  We classified 34 files: 17 data, 8 code, 8 documentation, 1 materials.
-  We found 17 tabular data files and extracted 297 columns from 17 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4). We ran automated data-quality checks on 297 columns; 16 columns have at least one potential issue (7 columns with numeric values stored as text; 6 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 4 columns with inconsistent category casing; 4 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column with no observed values (entirely empty)). 29 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (29 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 1 file is a Qualtrics survey export.

papers.title: Reconsidering Global Comparisons of Scientist Trustworthiness
papers.summary:
-  We classified 184 files: 40 data, 40 code, 6 documentation, 98 materials.
-  We found 40 tabular data files and extracted 862 columns from 13 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  8 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://osf.io/5c3qd exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, 2 files omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more.
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (ds_id.sav: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: ds_id.sav. We ran automated data-quality checks on 862 columns; 171 columns have at least one potential issue (154 columns with numeric values stored as text; 14 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 12 columns with inconsistent category casing; 12 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 12 columns whose values look like personal information; 4 columns with values in a legacy (non-UTF-8) encoding; 3 columns with no observed values (entirely empty)). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 2 of 2 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Speaking Progress, Feeling Threat: A Biopsychosocial Approach to Systemic Progressive Social Change
papers.summary:
-  We classified 56 files: 20 data, 2 code, 14 documentation, 8 materials, 10 output, 2 unknown.
-  We found 20 tabular data files and extracted 1096 columns from 18 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (overview?view_only=0be6dbcb31b14394a731fc47e99577bd: if it doesnt stress us were not changing the system_correlation table chapter 3.xlsx: 73% of columns are free text, not variables; hnf8b: if it doesnt stress us were not changing the system_correlation table chapter 3.xlsx: 73% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: overview?view_only=0be6dbcb31b14394a731fc47e99577bd: if it doesnt stress us were not changing the system_correlation table chapter 3.xlsx, hnf8b: if it doesnt stress us were not changing the system_correlation table chapter 3.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1096 columns; 68 columns have at least one potential issue (52 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 10 columns holding an SPSS "Select Cases" filter (analyses may have used only a subset of rows); 6 columns with inconsistent category casing). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 6 of 12 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Same stimuli, different spaces: how task, observer and amount of data influence geometry and reliability of mental representations
papers.summary:
-  We classified 1532 files: 1314 data, 48 code, 58 documentation, 111 materials, 1 unknown.
-  We found 509 tabular data files and extracted 12878 columns from 507 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (original_session_order.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; things_images.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: original_session_order.txt, things_images.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 12878 columns; 1473 columns have at least one potential issue (1473 columns with no observed values (entirely empty)). We detected demographic column for Gender.

papers.title: Task effects on predictive eye-movements
papers.summary:
-  We classified 35 files: 14 data, 6 code, 13 documentation, 2 materials.
-  We found 14 tabular data files and extracted 88 columns from 3 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 3 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  7 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (Recording_Notes_Attention_study_fillers.xlsx: 53% of columns are free text and 89% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: Recording_Notes_Attention_study_fillers.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 88 columns; 42 columns have at least one potential issue (15 columns with numeric values stored as text; 11 columns with inconsistent category casing; 10 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 7 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 2 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 1 column whose values look like personal information; 1 column with leading/trailing whitespace). 116 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (116 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). 4 of 4 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Does facial expression processing require attention? A multi-lab replication of Eimer et al. (2003)
papers.summary:
-  We classified 102 files: 22 data, 4 code, 2 documentation, 74 materials.
-  We found 22 tabular data files and extracted 96 columns from 12 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  10 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (counterbalance3.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; counterbalance8.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; counterbalance5.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; blocksEmotion.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; blocksLine.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; counterbalance1.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; counterbalance4.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; counterbalance6.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; counterbalance2.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; counterbalance7.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: counterbalance3.xlsx, counterbalance8.xlsx, counterbalance5.xlsx, blocksEmotion.xlsx, blocksLine.xlsx, counterbalance1.xlsx, counterbalance4.xlsx, counterbalance6.xlsx, counterbalance2.xlsx, counterbalance7.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 96 columns and found no issues. 10 of 22 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).
